Add time-to-event follow-up outcomes to a transplant cohort

Source: R/add_time_to_event_variables.R
add_txf_outcomes.Rd

Uses the cohort's file_key attribute (as set by load_srtr_file()) to load the matching follow-up file (TX_KI to TXF_KI, and so on), limited to the cohort's TRR_IDs and to the columns used here, and adds what the follow-up forms say about malignancy and acute rejection.

Usage

add_txf_outcomes(df)

Arguments

df

A transplant data frame from load_srtr_file(), with a TRR_ID column and a file_key attribute.

Value

df with these columns added. For TX_KP, each rejection column comes once per graft, with the suffix _KI or _PA (FIRST_FU_REJ_DATE_KI, FIRST_FU_REJ_STATUS_PA, ...); malignancy is patient-level and uses the forms for both grafts.

FIRST_FU_MALIG_DATE

Date of the first form reporting a malignancy (TFL_MALIG "Y").

FIRST_FU_MALIG_STATUS

What the forms say: "event" (at least one form reports a malignancy), "no event" (none does, and at least one says "N"), "unknown" (forms exist, but none says "Y" or "N"), or "no follow-up" (no form).

FIRST_FU_MALIG_LAST_NEG_DATE

Date of the last form saying "N", strictly before FIRST_FU_MALIG_DATE; with no report, the last such form at all.

FIRST_FU_REJ_DATE

Date of the first form reporting a treated acute rejection (TFL_ACUTE_REJ_EPISODE code 1 of format ACREJEPF, raw or labelled).

FIRST_FU_REJ_STATUS

"event" (a treated rejection), "untreated" (no treated rejection, but at least one untreated, code 2), "no event" (at least one form says no rejection, code 3), "unknown" (only code 998 or no answer), or "no follow-up".

FIRST_FU_REJ_LAST_NEG_DATE

Date of the last form saying no rejection (code 3), strictly before FIRST_FU_REJ_DATE; with no report, the last such form at all. An untreated rejection is evidence of rejection, so it is not a negative form.

The result also carries a txf_report attribute, a list of counts from the merge for a methods section. Counts are of transplant registrations (distinct TRR_IDs), not people, and of form rows:

follow_up_file

The follow-up file read, such as "TXF_KI".

cohort_rows

Rows of df.

registrations

Distinct non-missing TRR_IDs in df.

registrations_with_forms

Of those, how many have at least one follow-up form.

forms

Follow-up form rows for those registrations.

forms_undated

Of those, how many have no TFL_PX_STAT_DT.

outcomes

A tibble with one row per outcome ("malignancy", "rejection", or for TX_KP "rejection, kidney" and "rejection, pancreas"): column, the date column; positive_forms, forms reporting it; registrations_with_report, registrations with a positive form (status "event"); and registrations_with_dated_report, those with at least one dated positive form, the earliest of which gives the date column. An undated positive form cannot be ordered against the dated ones.

Forms with a missing TRR_ID match no registration and count nowhere. The report describes the cohort at the time of the merge: filtering the result afterwards does not update it.

Details

The dates are report dates. A follow-up form covers a period, and its date (TFL_PX_STAT_DT, the patient status date) is when the status was recorded, not when the malignancy or rejection began. The event happened at some time after the last negative form and on or before the first report, so ..._LAST_NEG_DATE and the report date bound it for interval-censored or discrete-time models. Whether that interval bounds clinical onset depends on what each form asked.

Evidence and timing are kept apart. A status of "event" with a missing date means a form reports the event but no positive form is dated; ..._LAST_NEG_DATE is then missing too, since the bound is unknown. A missing date alone does not mean no event: read the status column.

Forms for every period count here, whenever they are dated. add_time_to_event_outcomes() counts a report as an event only inside the follow-up window.

Combined organ codes in TXF_KP (ORG_TY other than KI or PA) cannot be assigned to one graft, and give a warning.

See also

add_time_to_event_outcomes(), srtr_time_to_event(), load_srtr_file()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
tx <- load_srtr_file("TX_KI")
tx <- add_txf_outcomes(tx)
table(tx$FIRST_FU_REJ_STATUS)
} # }
